symbols.name: git_churn
symbols.note: Runs git log --numstat; returns dict of added+deleted per file, or {} on failure.

symbols.name: _parse_numstat
symbols.note: Parses git log --numstat output; handles binary files and renames.

symbols.name: _rename_target
symbols.note: Resolves git rename notation to new path.

symbols.name: COCHANGE_MAX_FILES_PER_COMMIT
symbols.note: Maximum files per commit for co-change analysis; commits exceeding this are dropped.

claims.text: ``git_churn`` returns per-file add+delete line totals summed over history (optionally a recent window)
claims.why: git_churn returns dict[str,int] and accepts since parameter; docstring matches code.

claims.text: Degrades cleanly and completely: not a git repo, git not on PATH, timeout, or any parse hiccup -> ``{}``
claims.why: git_churn catches OSError and subprocess.SubprocessError, returns {}; also checks returncode.

claims.text: Windows-safe: UTF-8 with ``errors='replace'`` and a hard timeout.
claims.why: subprocess.run uses encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', and timeout parameter.

claims.text: ``co_change_pairs``/``temporal_misses`` (below) are a SEPARATE analysis over the SAME log data, added alongside ``git_churn`` rather than folded into it
claims.why: temporal_misses not defined in this chunk; co_change_pairs is partial.

claims.text: ``git_churn``'s return shape and degradation contract are relied on by ``index.py:511`` and must stay exactly as they are.
Runs ``git -C <root> log --numstat --format=`` (empty format => only the numstat body).
``since`` (e.g. '3 months ago', '2025-01-01') narrows to a recent window
claims.why: If since is truthy, cmd appends f'--since={since}'.

claims.text: Returns ``{}`` on any failure so the caller can treat churn as optional.
claims.why: Exceptions and non-zero returncode both return {}.
If added_s.isdigit() is False, added = 0; same for deleted.

claims.text: Rename lines (``old => new`` or ``dir/{old => new}/file``) are normalized to the NEW path so churn follows the file across renames.
claims.why: _parse_numstat calls _rename_target on each path before accumulating.

claims.text: Resolve git's rename notation to the current (new) path. ``a/{old => new}/f.py`` -> ``a/new/f.py``;  ``old.py => new.py`` -> ``new.py``.
claims.why: Code uses regex for {} and =>, extracts new path.

claims.text: A commit touching more files than this is DROPPED ENTIRELY from co-change -- not truncated, excluded -- because a mass reformat / vendor bump / squash merge produces C(n,2) pairs (a 200-file commit is ~19,900 pairs) that are pure noise, not coupling, and are expensive to even enumerate.
claims.why: The constant is defined, but the logic to drop commits is not in this chunk; co_change_pairs body missing.

claims.text: 40 sits well above a normal focused commit (this repo's own history reliably stays in the single digits to low teens of files per commit) and well below a repo-wide sweep
claims.why: No way to verify repo history from this chunk.

claims.text: Runs its OWN ``git log --numstat --format=%H`` (a separate invocation from ``git_churn``, which intentionally keeps its empty ``--format=`` -- see the module docstring).
claims.why: Function body not present; cannot confirm command construction.

claims.text: ``%H`` makes commits separable so co-occurrence can be computed per commit instead of over one undifferentiated numstat stream.
Each commit's file set is capped at ``max_files_per_commit``; a commit over the cap is dropped entirely (see ``COCHANGE_MAX_FILES_PER_COMMIT``).
Weighted by PMI (``ln(N * count_ab / (count_a * count_b))``) and lift (``exp(pmi)``), not raw co-occurrence count
claims.why: Calculation not present in this chunk.
